headline: Bond revolts, Hormuz shock and Taiwan quarantine usher in an era of financial repression

events: French government falls over budget; OAT-Bund spread blows past 200bp and ECB activates TPI for the first time, with conditionality fights splitting the Governing Council
UK gilt sell-off forces emergency fiscal statement with deep capital-spending cuts; 30-year yields touch 6.3%
US imposes semiconductor-equipment and pharma tariffs; China retaliates with expanded rare-earth and gallium export licensing
Record South Asian heatwave and failed monsoon push global rice and wheat prices up ~30%; Egypt, Pakistan and Kenya seek emergency IMF financing
AI capex boom continues but first large write-downs at second-tier data-centre lessors spook credit markets
Iran-Israel exchange escalates into tanker attacks and partial Hormuz closure for seven weeks; Brent spikes to $148 and European gas triples
G20 inflation peaks above 7%; central banks hike into weakness, US policy rate reaches 5.75%
Weak US 10-year and 30-year Treasury auctions during a contested election-year debt-ceiling standoff; 10-year yield hits 6.4% before the Fed launches a 'market functioning' purchase facility
Pakistan, Egypt, Argentina and Nigeria default or restructure; Common Framework overwhelmed
Global recession begins in Q4 as AI-equity correction of ~35% hits wealth effects and credit spreads widen
Global GDP contracts ~0.8%; unemployment peaks near 7% globally, above 9% in the euro periphery
China declares a 'customs quarantine' on Taiwan after island election; US-allied navies escort convoys, chip shipments fall 40% for five months before a tense modus vivendi
Japan's BoJ caps JGB yields again as life insurers dump foreign bonds; yen swings destabilise Asian FX
Italy and Belgium enter ECB-backed adjustment programmes; Turkey and South Africa face sovereign crises
Firms accelerate AI-driven back-office automation to cut costs; layoffs in finance, call centres and admin swell displacement figures
Financial repression becomes the norm: US Treasury-Fed accord caps 10-year yields at ~4.5%, banks and pension funds face higher domestic-bond holding requirements across G7
Inflation settles at 4-5% as negative real rates erode debt; middle-class savers and renters lose ground while asset owners recover
Sahel-to-Gulf-of-Guinea insurgency widens and a Serbia-Kosovo armed clash draws NATO peacekeepers in
Energy security drive spurs record solar and battery deployment in Europe, India and China, while US and Gulf expand LNG
Populist governments win in three G7 countries; wealth taxes and windfall levies spread
Weak, uneven recovery: world growth ~2.6%, but debt ratios higher after recession and defence spending surge to 3%+ of GDP in NATO
Ukraine frozen-conflict armistice holds shakily; Middle East remains a source of recurring oil scares
Successive climate disasters (Category 5 hurricane on the US Gulf Coast, Mediterranean megafires) trigger home-insurance market exits and state backstops
Trade organised in rival blocs with managed 'trusted partner' corridors; WTO dispute system defunct
AI adoption broadens to about a third of firms, mostly for cost-cutting rather than new growth

winners: Commodity and LNG exporters with strong balance sheets (Norway, Gulf states, Canada, Australia)
India and Mexico as 'trusted-corridor' manufacturing hubs
Leveraged real-asset owners benefiting from negative real rates
losers: Indebted frontier economies in Africa and South Asia
Euro periphery workers and savers under adjustment programmes
Renters and young people in advanced economies
Taiwan-dependent electronics supply chains and small exporters
bullets: Advanced economies run de facto yield caps and financial repression; inflation of 3.5-4.5% quietly erodes debt but not fast enough to stop ratios rising.
Global public debt has climbed to ~113% of GDP after a 2028-29 recession, energy subsidies and a rearmament wave.
Nine sovereign debt crises since 2027, including two euro-area programmes, have left a patchwork of IMF-, ECB- and China-led restructurings.
Trade is split into US-aligned and China-aligned blocs; tariffs and export controls are permanent features, and the Taiwan quarantine left chip supply chains doubled and costly.
Climate damage is visibly worse at ~1.6C: insurance retreat, food-price volatility and heat migration feed instability, even as renewables reach ~43% of electricity.
AI diffuses steadily but mainly as a cost-cutting tool in recession, displacing ~40 million jobs cumulatively and deepening white-collar anxiety.
Trust in institutions is near record lows; populist and nationalist parties govern or co-govern in much of the G7, and protests over cost of living are routine.
Recovery under way by 2031 but fragile, with markets one oil or bond shock away from another episode.
wildcard: China's 2029 'customs quarantine' of Taiwan, halting a large share of advanced-chip exports for five months without open war.
image_description: In a rain-soaked Milan street in 2031, a queue of commuters waits at a solar-powered bus shelter plastered with protest posters about pension cuts, while a delivery robot squeezes past a shuttered bank branch advertising 'patriotic savings bonds'.
